claim: In solid tumors, targeted treatments can lead to dramatic regressions, but responses are often short-lived because resistant cancer cells arise.
source_text: In solid tumors, targeted treatments can lead to dramatic regressions, but responses are often short-lived because resistant cancer cells arise.
evidence_reasoning: This is a general statement about the clinical behavior of solid tumors that reflects established scientific consensus and is supported by citations throughout the manuscript.

claim: The major strategy proposed for overcoming resistance is combination therapy.
source_text: The major strategy proposed for overcoming resistance is combination therapy.
evidence_reasoning: This reflects established scientific consensus about therapeutic strategies for cancer resistance.

claim: Dual therapy results in long-term disease control for most patients, if there are no single mutations that cause cross-resistance to both drugs.
source_text: We find that dual therapy results in long-term disease control for most patients, if there are no single mutations that cause cross-resistance to both drugs
evidence_reasoning: This is a primary finding from the mathematical model and simulations presented in the study.

claim: In patients with large disease burden, triple therapy is needed.
source_text: in patients with large disease burden, triple therapy is needed
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is derived from the mathematical modeling and analysis of patient data presented in the study.

claim: Simultaneous therapy with two drugs is much more effective than sequential therapy.
source_text: We also find that simultaneous therapy with two drugs is much more effective than sequential therapy.
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from the mathematical model comparing simultaneous vs sequential treatment strategies.

claim: Imatinib was successful in the treatment of chronic myeloid leukemia (CML).

evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to Druker et al., 2006 and Gambacorti-Passerini et al., 2011, and represents established clinical knowledge.

claim: Four decades of research passed between the discovery of the Philadelphia chromosome and the first treatment to target an activated oncogene in a human cancer.
source_text: Four decades of research passed between the discovery of the Philadelphia chromosome and the first treatment to target an activated oncogene in a human cancer.
evidence_reasoning: This is a historical fact about the timeline of cancer research.

source_text: vemurafenib for patients with melanomas harboring BRAF mutations

evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Kwak et al., 2010 and represents established clinical knowledge.

source_text: In most patients with solid tumors, the cancer evolves to become resistant within a few months

claim: A small number of cells resistant to any targeted agent are always present in large solid tumors at the start of therapy.

claim: Resistant cells clonally expand once therapy is administered.
source_text: these cells clonally expand once therapy is administered

claim: Tumor recurrences are a fait accompli when single agents are delivered.
source_text: Tumor recurrences are thus a fait accompli when single agents are delivered

claim: The model is based on a multitype branching process.
source_text: Our model is based on a multitype branching process
evidence_reasoning: This describes the mathematical framework used in the study.

claim: Mathematical modeling has successfully predicted the dynamics of acquired resistance in colorectal cancer patients treated with panitumumab.
source_text: Similar mathematical modeling has successfully predicted the dynamics of acquired resistance, including the timing of treatment failure, in colorectal cancer patients treated with the EGFR inhibitor panitumumab

claim: Mathematical modeling has led to specific recommendations for combination therapies to treat CML.
source_text: has led to specific recommendations for combination therapies to treat CML
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to Komarova et al., 2009 and Katouli and Komarova, 2010.

claim: The study analyzed the dynamics of 68 index lesions in 20 melanoma patients receiving vemurafenib.
source_text: To obtain key parameters for our model, we have studied the dynamics of 68 index lesions in 20 melanoma patients receiving the BRAF inhibitor vemurafenib.
evidence_reasoning: This describes the clinical data collected and analyzed in the study.

claim: For 21 lesions in the vemurafenib dataset, two pretreatment measurements were available.
source_text: For 21 lesions in our vemurafenib dataset, two pretreatment measurements were available.
evidence_reasoning: This describes the data available for analysis.

claim: The average net growth rate of melanoma lesions is 0.01 per day.
source_text: Using these data, we calculate the average net growth rate of these lesions to be 0.01 per day
evidence_reasoning: This is calculated from the clinical data collected in the study.

claim: The calculated net growth rate of 0.01 per day is consistent with previous reports.
source_text: which is consistent with previous reports
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to Friberg and Mattson, 1997 and Eskelin et al., 2000.

claim: The estimated average time between cell divisions in melanoma cells is 7 days.
source_text: The estimated average time between cell divisions in the absence of cell death in melanoma cells is 7 days
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Rew and Wilson, 2000.

claim: The birth (cell division) rate is 0.14 per day.
source_text: implying a birth (cell division) rate of b = 0.14 per day
evidence_reasoning: This is calculated from the time between cell divisions.

claim: The cell death rate is set to d = b − 0.01 to achieve the observed net growth rate.
source_text: To achieve the observed net growth rate, we set the cell death rate to d = b − 0.01 (typical d = 0.13)
evidence_reasoning: This is calculated to match the observed net growth rate.

claim: A cell type is defined as sensitive if the treatment would cause its death rate to exceed its birth rate.
source_text: A cell type is defined as sensitive if the treatment in question would cause its death rate to exceed its birth rate
evidence_reasoning: This is a definition established for the mathematical model.

claim: If a cell type is not sensitive, it is resistant.
source_text: otherwise, it is resistant
evidence_reasoning: This is a definition established for the mathematical model.

claim: The point mutation rate is approximately 10^-9 for most cancers.
source_text: where s = 1 − d/b is the survival probability of the branching process initiated with a single cell and u is the point mutation rate, ∼10−9 for most cancers
evidence_reasoning: This represents established knowledge about mutation rates in cancer.

claim: If there is at least one possible mutation that could confer resistance to both drugs, the expected number of cells resistant to both drugs is X ≈ M n12 µ.
source_text: If there is at least one possible mutation that could in principle confer resistance to both drugs, n12 ≥ 1, then X ≈ M n12 µ.
evidence_reasoning: This is derived from the mathematical model.

claim: When n12 ≥ 1, the expected number of cells resistant to both drugs is independent of the numbers of mutations that confer resistance to each individual drug.
source_text: In this case, the expected number of cells resistant to both drugs is independent of the numbers of mutations, n1 and n2, that have the potential to confer resistance to each individual drug.
evidence_reasoning: This is a mathematical result from the model.

claim: Tumor cells are much more likely to become resistant to dual therapy through one mutation conferring resistance to both drugs than through sequential mutations conferring resistance to each drug separately.
source_text: Intuitively, this means that tumor cells are much more likely to become resistant to dual therapy through the occurrence of one mutation conferring resistance to both drugs simultaneously than through sequential mutations conferring resistance to each drug separately.
evidence_reasoning: This is an interpretation of the mathematical results.

claim: If there is no mutation that could confer resistance to both drugs simultaneously, then X ≈ M n1n2 µ^2.
source_text: If there is no mutation that could confer resistance to both drugs simultaneously (no cross-resistance), then n12 = 0 and we obtain X ≈ M n1n2 µ2.
evidence_reasoning: This is derived from the mathematical model.

claim: When n12 = 0, the number of resistant cells scales with the square of the point mutation rate.
source_text: This quantity scales with the square of the point mutation rate, so the number of resistant cells in a tumor will be much smaller than for the case n12 > 0.
evidence_reasoning: This is a mathematical consequence of the formula X ≈ M n1n2 µ^2.

claim: The expected number of cells resistant to combination therapy with k drugs, with no cross-resistance, is X ≈ M n1n2 … nk µ^k.
source_text: In general, the expected number of cells resistant to combination therapy with k drugs, with no cross-resistance, is X ≈ M n1n2 … nk µk
evidence_reasoning: This is a generalization of the mathematical model to k drugs.

claim: Resistance is the outcome of random mutation, division, and death events.
source_text: We emphasize, however, that resistance is the outcome of random mutation, division, and death events
evidence_reasoning: This reflects the stochastic nature of the biological process being modeled.

claim: Resistance may arise in one lesion but not in another, even if these lesions are otherwise identical.
source_text: and consequently may arise in one lesion but not in another, even if these lesions are otherwise identical
evidence_reasoning: This is a consequence of the stochastic nature of resistance development.

claim: The 68 lesions in the dataset declined at median rate b′ − d′ = −0.03 per day during treatment.
source_text: To obtain estimates for the birth rate b′ and death rate d′ of sensitive cells during treatment, we calculate that the 68 lesions in our dataset declined at median rate b′ − d′ = −0.03 per day
evidence_reasoning: This is calculated from the clinical data.

claim: The 10th and 90th percentile decline rates during treatment were −0.01 and −0.07 per day, respectively.
source_text: (−0.01 and −0.07 being 10th and 90th percentile, respectively)
evidence_reasoning: This is calculated from the clinical data.

claim: Resistant cells maintain the pretreatment birth and death rates during treatment.
source_text: We assume that resistant cells maintain the pretreatment birth and death rates, b and d, respectively, during treatment.
evidence_reasoning: This is an assumption of the mathematical model.

claim: Treatment failure can be caused by the preexistence of resistance to both drugs in a small number of tumor cells.
source_text: In summary, treatment failure can be caused either by the preexistence of resistance to both drugs in a small number of tumor cells
evidence_reasoning: This is a conclusion from the model simulations.

claim: Treatment failure can be caused by the emergence of resistant cells during treatment.
source_text: or the emergence of resistant cells during treatment
evidence_reasoning: This is a conclusion from the model simulations.

claim: The therapy is successful if there is no resistant lineage arising in any of four scenarios: 1-step resistance before treatment, 1-step resistance during treatment, 2-step resistance before treatment, or 2-step resistance during treatment.
source_text: The therapy is successful if there is no resistant lineage arising in any of these four scenarios
evidence_reasoning: This is derived from the mathematical model structure.

claim: The overall success probability is obtained by multiplying the probabilities of no resistance in each of the four independent scenarios.
source_text: since these are independent events, the overall success probability is obtained by multiplying the corresponding probabilities
evidence_reasoning: This follows from probability theory for independent events.

claim: A single mutation conferring cross-resistance to both drugs can prohibit any hope for successful dual therapy.
source_text: A single mutation conferring cross-resistance to both drugs (n12 = 1) can prohibit any hope for a successful dual therapy.
evidence_reasoning: This is a conclusion from the mathematical model and simulations shown in Figure 3.

claim: Most patients with advanced cancers have multiple lesions.
source_text: Although modeling of single neoplastic lesions is the norm in theoretical studies, most patients with advanced cancers have multiple lesions
evidence_reasoning: This is established clinical knowledge.

claim: Curing a patient requires eradication of all lesions.
source_text: curing a patient requires eradication of all lesions
evidence_reasoning: This is established clinical knowledge.

claim: The study quantified all radiographically detectable metastases in 22 patients: 7 with pancreatic ductal adenocarcinomas, 11 with colorectal carcinomas, and 6 with melanomas.
source_text: To determine the total extent of disease in typical patients who enroll for clinical trials, we quantified all radiographically detectable metastases in 22 such patients: 7 with pancreatic ductal adenocarcinomas, 11 with colorectal carcinomas, and 6 with melanomas
evidence_reasoning: This describes the clinical data collected in the study.

claim: The number of metastatic lesions in the 22 patients ranged from 1 to 30.
source_text: The number of metastatic lesions in the 22 patients described in Table 1 ranged from 1 to 30
evidence_reasoning: This is data from the patient cohort analyzed.

claim: The total tumor burden in the 22 patients ranged from 9 × 10^8 to 3 × 10^11 cells.
source_text: and their total tumor burden ranged from 9 × 108 to 3 × 1011 cells
evidence_reasoning: This is data from the patient cohort analyzed.

claim: Monotherapy will fail in all 22 patients analyzed.
source_text: We find that monotherapy will fail in all 22 patients
evidence_reasoning: This is a prediction from the mathematical model applied to the patient data.

claim: If there is even one possible mutation that can confer resistance to both drugs, dual therapy has only a small chance of curing patients.
source_text: If there is even one possible mutation that can in principle confer resistance to both drugs, then our model shows that dual therapy has also only a small chance of curing patients, even those with the smallest tumor burden.
evidence_reasoning: This is a prediction from the mathematical model.

claim: When n12 = 1, none of the 22 patients are expected to be cured with dual therapy.
source_text: In our cohort of 22 patients, none are expected to be cured under these circumstances
evidence_reasoning: This is a prediction from the mathematical model applied to the patient data.

claim: Only if there are no potential mutations that can confer cross-resistance will dual therapy be successful in eradicating all lesions.
source_text: Only if there are no potential mutations that can confer cross-resistance will dual therapy be successful in eradicating all lesions.
evidence_reasoning: This is a conclusion from the mathematical model.

claim: Eight patients with the smallest tumor burden would have >95% probability of cure with dual therapy when n12 = 0.
source_text: In the cohort described in Table 1, we calculate that eight patients (those with the smallest tumor burden) would have >95% probability of cure.
evidence_reasoning: This is a prediction from the mathematical model applied to the patient data.

claim: Patients with the largest tumor burden would have a >20% probability of tumor recurrence even with dual therapy when n12 = 0.
source_text: Those with the largest tumor burden would still have a >20% probability of tumor recurrence.
evidence_reasoning: This is a prediction from the mathematical model applied to the patient data.

claim: Therapy with three agents will not cure patients if there is even one mutation that can confer resistance to all three agents.
source_text: Additional simulations show that therapy with three agents will also not cure patients if there is even one mutation that can confer resistance to all three agents.
evidence_reasoning: This is a prediction from simulations extending the model to three drugs.

claim: In patients whose tumors have high cell turnover (time between cell divisions of 1 day), even dual therapy with no cross-resistance mutations would be expected to fail in 37% of patients.
source_text: We note that in patients whose tumors have high cell turnover (time between cell divisions of 1 day, corresponding to b = 1), even dual therapy with no cross-resistance mutations would be expected to fail in 37% of patients described in Table 1
evidence_reasoning: This is a prediction from the model with different parameter values.

claim: In current clinical practice, it is common to administer targeted agents sequentially.
source_text: In current clinical practice, it is common to administer targeted agents sequentially: once relapse occurs, a second, often experimental, agent is administered.
evidence_reasoning: This describes current clinical practice.

claim: When there is a possibility of a single mutation conferring resistance to both drugs, sequential combination therapy will always fail.
source_text: When there is a possibility of a single mutation conferring resistance to both drugs, sequential combination therapy will 'always' fail.
evidence_reasoning: This is a prediction from the mathematical model.

claim: In approximately 74% of lesions treated sequentially, failure is due to mutations present prior to treatment with the first drug.
source_text: In ∼74% of lesions, the failure is due to mutations that were present prior to the treatment with the first drug
evidence_reasoning: This is a result from the model simulations.

claim: In approximately 26% of lesions treated sequentially, failure is due to the development of cells resistant to drug 2 during treatment with drug 1.
source_text: whereas in ∼26% of the lesions, failure is due to the development of cells resistant to drug 2 during treatment with drug 1
evidence_reasoning: This is a result from the model simulations.

claim: With simultaneous therapy, 26.3% of patients can be cured when n12 = 1.
source_text: With simultaneous therapy, 26.3% of patients can be cured under the same circumstances.
evidence_reasoning: This is a result from the model simulations comparing simultaneous vs sequential therapy.

claim: If the two drugs have no resistance mutations in common (n12 = 0), simultaneous therapy is successful with a probability of 99.9%.
source_text: If the two drugs have no resistance mutations in common (n12 = 0), then simultaneous therapy is successful with a probability of 99.9%
evidence_reasoning: This is a result from the model simulations.

claim: When n12 = 0, sequential therapy still fails in all cases.
source_text: while sequential therapy still fails in all cases
evidence_reasoning: This is a result from the model simulations.

claim: Evidence to date does not indicate that cancer stem cells are innately resistant to either single drugs or drug combinations.
source_text: Evidence to date does not indicate that cancer stem cells are innately resistant to either single drugs or drug combinations.
evidence_reasoning: This reflects current scientific understanding about cancer stem cells.

claim: The precise proportion of cancer stem cells has a dramatic effect on the development of resistance.
source_text: However, the precise proportion of cancer stem cells (among all cancer cells) has a dramatic effect on the development of resistance.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference from the model when considering cancer stem cell dynamics.

claim: If cancer stem cells represent only 0.1% of cancer cells, the development of resistance is roughly 0.1% as likely as if 100% of cancer cells can repopulate the tumor.
source_text: For example, if cancer stem cells represent only 0.1% of cancer cells, then the development of resistance to single agents or combinations is roughly 0.1% as likely as if 100% of the cancer cells have the capacity to repopulate the tumor.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference from applying the model to cancer stem cell scenarios.

claim: The fraction of cancer stem cells in CML appears to be low, perhaps explaining the remarkable success of imatinib.
source_text: The fraction of cancer stem cells appears to be this low in CML, perhaps explaining the remarkable success of imatinib
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference supported by citation to Michor et al., 2005.

claim: In solid tumors, the fraction of cancer stem cells seems much higher, usually higher than 5% and in some cases close to 100%.
source_text: In solid tumors, however, the fraction of cancer stem cells seems much higher, usually higher than 5% and in some cases close to 100%
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Shackleton et al., 2009.

claim: Non-stem cells can convert to cancer stem cells under certain conditions.
source_text: This issue is further complicated by the fact that the situation is plastic, with non-stem cells converting to cancer stem cells under certain conditions
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Gupta et al., 2009.

claim: If resistance has a fitness cost, there will be a smaller number of resistant cells at the start of treatment and a higher chance of treatment success.
source_text: If resistance has a fitness cost, then we expect a smaller number of resistant cells at the start of treatment and correspondingly a higher chance of treatment success.
evidence_reasoning: This is a logical inference about the effect of costly resistance.

claim: For combination therapies with drugs that have resistance mutations in common, the probability of eradicating a lesion is only marginally affected by costly resistance.
source_text: For combination therapies with drugs that have resistance mutations in common, the probability of eradicating a lesion is only marginally affected by costly resistance.
evidence_reasoning: This is a result from computer simulations shown in Table 2.

claim: For dual therapies with no cross-resistance mutations, treatment has a high chance of eradicating all but the largest lesions, whether or not resistance is costly.
source_text: For dual therapies with no cross-resistance mutations, treatment has a high chance of eradicating all but the largest lesions, whether or not resistance is costly.
evidence_reasoning: This is a result from computer simulations shown in Table 2.

claim: If each resistance mutation decreases the net growth rate of cells by 10%, the probability that dual therapy with no cross-resistance mutations will eradicate a lesion of size 10^11 with daily cell division is 68%.
source_text: For example, if each resistance mutation decreases the net growth rate of cells by 10%, the probability that dual therapy with no cross-resistance mutations will eradicate a lesion of size 1011 in which cells divide on average every day is 68%
evidence_reasoning: This is a result from computer simulations.

claim: Without costly resistance, the probability of eradicating a lesion of size 10^11 with daily cell division is 47%.
source_text: (compared with 47% in the case of neutral resistance)
evidence_reasoning: This is a result from computer simulations for comparison.

claim: Some therapies may directly eliminate tumor cells (d′ > d), whereas others may impede their division (b′ < b).
source_text: Some therapies may directly eliminate tumor cells (d′ > d), whereas others may impede their division (b′ < b).
evidence_reasoning: This describes different mechanisms of action for cancer therapies.

claim: The rate b′ − d′ of tumor decline is of primary importance, and whether this is achieved by eliminating cells or suppressing division has only a minor effect on treatment outcomes.
source_text: Overall, the rate b′ − d′ of tumor decline is of primary importance, and whether this is achieved by eliminating cells or suppressing division has only a minor effect on treatment outcomes.
evidence_reasoning: This is a conclusion from the mathematical analysis.

claim: If therapy shrinks a tumor at rate −0.03 per day by increasing cell death, the eradication probability is 26% for a specific scenario.
source_text: For example, consider a dual therapy with n1 = n2 = 50, n12 = 1, applied to a lesion of size M = 109, with other parameters as inferred from our dataset. If this therapy shrinks the tumor at rate −0.03 per day by increasing cell death, the eradication probability is 26%.
evidence_reasoning: This is a result from the mathematical model for a specific example.

claim: If therapy shrinks a tumor at rate −0.03 per day by suppressing division instead, the eradication probability increases to 29%.
source_text: If the therapy instead suppresses division, this probability increases to 29%
evidence_reasoning: This is a result from the mathematical model for comparison.

claim: The suppression of division leads to fewer chances for resistance mutations during treatment.
source_text: because there are fewer chances for resistance mutations during treatment
evidence_reasoning: This is the explanation for why suppressing division is slightly more effective.

claim: The analytical results can accommodate parameter values from any type of cancer, once they become available.
source_text: While our typical parameter values are derived from the melanoma dataset, our analytical results can accommodate parameter values from any other type of cancer, once they become available.
evidence_reasoning: This describes the generalizability of the mathematical framework.

claim: The results are qualitatively robust across a wide range of birth and death rates.
source_text: Furthermore, our results are qualitatively robust across a wide range of birth and death rates
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated in Supplementary file 3.

claim: The parameters with the strongest effects on the success of combination treatments are lesion sizes and point mutation rate, apart from the number of cross-resistance mutations.
source_text: The parameters with the strongest effects on the success of combination treatments—apart from the number of cross-resistance mutations—are lesion sizes and point mutation rate.
evidence_reasoning: This is a conclusion from the sensitivity analysis of the model.

claim: Combination treatments will be more effective in cancers with small fractions of tumor stem cells.
source_text: Thus, we expect that combination treatments will be more effective in cancers with small fractions of tumor stem cells (small effective population size of lesions)
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference from the model about the effect of effective population size.

claim: Combination treatments will be less effective in cancers with significantly increased point mutation rates.
source_text: and less effective in cancers with significantly increased point mutation rates
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference from the model about the effect of mutation rate.

claim: If there is one genetic alteration that can confer resistance to two targeted agents, therapy with those agents will not result in sustained benefit for the majority of patients with advanced disease.
source_text: Most importantly, they show that even if there is one genetic alteration within any of the 6.6 billion base pairs present in a human diploid cell that can confer resistance to two targeted agents, therapy with those agents will not result in sustained benefit for the majority of patients with advanced disease.
evidence_reasoning: This is a primary conclusion from the study.

claim: The same result is obtained with triple therapy; if there is the possibility of a mutation conferring cross-resistance to three drugs, lesions will always recur.
source_text: The same result is obtained with triple therapy; if there is the possibility of a mutation conferring cross-resistance to three drugs, lesions of the size commonly observed in patients with advanced cancers will always recur.
evidence_reasoning: This is a conclusion from extending the model to three drugs.

claim: Komarova et al. (2009) showed that a combination of three current targeted drugs for CML will not be beneficial over a combination of two such drugs due to cross-resistance.
source_text: Similar conclusions were reached by Komarova et al. (2009), who showed that a combination of three current targeted drugs for CML will not be beneficial over a combination of two such drugs due to cross-resistance.
evidence_reasoning: This cites a previous study with similar conclusions.

claim: The development of drugs that act through distinct pathways will be essential for the success of combination therapies in the clinic.
source_text: The development of drugs that act through distinct pathways will therefore be essential for the success of combination therapies in the clinic.
evidence_reasoning: This is a conclusion drawn from the study's findings.

claim: The increased expression of growth factors (such as hepatocyte growth factor) can confer resistance to a variety of drugs that inhibit kinases functioning through different pathways.

evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to Straussman et al., 2012 and Wilson et al., 2012.

claim: Mutations in several different genes, including those encoding ABC transporters, can confer resistance to many different drugs.
source_text: Moreover, it is well known that mutations in several different genes, including those encoding ABC transporters, can confer resistance to many different drugs
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Lavi et al., 2012 and represents established knowledge.

claim: Drugs that have very different chemical structures, in addition to distinct mechanisms of action, may be required to circumvent resistance mechanisms.
source_text: Drugs that have very different chemical structures, in addition to distinct mechanisms of action, may be required to circumvent these resistance mechanisms.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative suggestion about future drug development strategies.

claim: The results are not readily applicable to therapies that rely on the immune destruction of tumors.
source_text: Our results are not readily applicable to therapies that rely on the immune destruction of tumors
evidence_reasoning: This is a limitation of the model acknowledged by the authors.

claim: The immune system, unlike small molecule compounds, can replicate and evolve.
source_text: The immune system, unlike small molecule compounds, can replicate and evolve
evidence_reasoning: This is established biological knowledge.

claim: The factors underlying therapeutic success or failure of immune modulators are not sufficiently understood to allow useful modeling at this point.
source_text: and the factors underlying therapeutic success or failure are not sufficiently understood to allow useful modeling at this point
evidence_reasoning: This reflects the current state of scientific understanding.

claim: Long-term control of disease is more common with immune modulators than with small molecule drugs.
source_text: it will be important to try to understand why long-term control of disease is more common with these therapies than with small molecule drugs
evidence_reasoning: This is an observation about clinical outcomes with different therapy types.

claim: The results on sequential vs simultaneous therapy are in agreement with previous results.
source_text: Our results on sequential vs simultaneous therapy with two or more agents (Figure 5) are in agreement with previous results
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Katouli and Komarova, 2011.

claim: Sequential administration of targeted agents is often used to treat patients, for a variety of medical and economic reasons.
source_text: Sequential administration of targeted agents is often used to treat patients, for a variety of medical and economic reasons.
evidence_reasoning: This describes current clinical practice.

claim: Sequential administration precludes any chance for cure, even when there are no possible mutations that can confer cross-resistance.
source_text: Our data show that this sequential administration precludes any chance for cure—even when there are no possible mutations that can confer cross-resistance

claim: When there are potential mutations conferring cross-resistance to two or more agents, simultaneous administration offers some hope for cure while there is no hope with sequential therapy.
source_text: And when there are potential mutations conferring cross-resistance to two or more agents, simultaneous administration offers some hope for cure while there is no hope with sequential therapy

claim: The realization of the advantages of simultaneous vs sequential dual therapy will hopefully stimulate efforts to combine agents much earlier in the drug development process.
source_text: The realization of the advantages of simultaneous vs sequential dual therapy will hopefully stimulate efforts to combine agents much earlier in the drug development process.

claim: Tumor growth and evolution is modeled as a continuous time multitype branching process.
source_text: We model tumor growth and evolution as a continuous time multitype branching process

claim: The model includes two phases: pretreatment and treatment.
source_text: Our model includes two phases: pretreatment and treatment.
evidence_reasoning: This describes the structure of the mathematical model.

claim: The pretreatment phase is initiated with a single fully sensitive cell.
source_text: The pretreatment phase is initiated with a single fully sensitive cell (type 00 for two drugs).

claim: During the pretreatment phase, all cell types reproduce at rate b and die at rate d.
source_text: During this phase, all cell types reproduce at rate b and die at rate d.

claim: The pretreatment phase ends when there are a total of M cells.
source_text: The pretreatment phase ends, and the treatment phase begins, when there are a total of M cells.

claim: During the treatment phase, all cell types that are sensitive to one or more drugs have birth rate b' and death rate d'.
source_text: During the treatment phase, all cell types that are sensitive to one or more drugs have birth rate b' and death rate d'
evidence_reasoning: This describes the dynamics during treatment in the mathematical model.

claim: Monte Carlo computer simulations are used to confirm analytical results and improve understanding of evolutionary dynamics during cancer treatment.
